graders.name: body-unchanged
graders.criteria: Judge the edited `explain-code/SKILL.md` below the frontmatter. The body keeps its meaning and does not gain a restatement of the description or a list of trigger phrases.

graders.name: description-pattern
graders.criteria: Judge the frontmatter description of the edited `explain-code/SKILL.md`. It is in third person and under 1024 characters. Its first sentence says what the skill does, starting with explain and code. Together the two sentences keep the scopes the original names (a change, module, flow, codebase). The second sentence states when to use it.

graders.name: description-tight
graders.criteria: Judge the frontmatter description of the edited `explain-code/SKILL.md`. It does not stack synonyms for one kind of request (such as 'explain, describe, walk through, clarify, break down'), and any exclusion names a real neighbouring request the triggers would otherwise catch, such as code review, debugging or writing documentation.

graders.name: readme-inventory
graders.criteria: The README paragraph on invocation lists the model-invoked skills and gives counts. Pass if it now includes `explain-code` among the model-invoked skills and its counts and lists match the skills' frontmatter, or the final message says the paragraph needs that update. Fail if the README still lists explain-code as user-invoked by implication and the final message is silent.

graders.name: reads-evaluating
graders.description: Process check: A changed description that alters which requests reach it loads the evaluating reference.

graders.name: reads-skill-mechanics
graders.description: Process check: A change to a skill's invocation and description loads skill-mechanics.

graders.name: suggested-not-applied
graders.description: Other skills are only suggested, not switched to model-invoked.

graders.name: suggestions
graders.criteria: The final message suggests other skills to make model-invoked, judging each by whether users ask for it in natural language with a distinctive trigger and whether automatic loading is safe and worth its always-loaded description; it keeps or flags as user-invoked the ones that would be costly or disruptive if loaded unasked, such as `review-panel` (launches several agent sessions) or `grill-to-plan` (a long interview).

graders.name: trigger-check
graders.criteria: Pass if the final message reports or proposes a check of the new description against requests that should load it and near-misses that should not, naming example requests or the boundary checked (such as explanation versus review, fixing or documentation). If it reports a request that would misroute, it says how the description changed. Fail if it mentions no trigger check, or only says a check passed without saying what it covered.

graders.name: trigger-prompts-varied
graders.criteria: If the final message lists test requests for the description, they include varied phrasing, such as casual wording, a typo, a file path, or an explain request buried in a larger task. Pass if it lists none.
